definition: Domain driven data mining is a data mining methodology for discovering actionable knowledge and deliver actionable insights from complex data and behaviors in a complex environment.
details: It studies the corresponding foundations, frameworks, algorithms, models, architectures, and evaluation systems for actionable knowledge discovery. Data-driven pattern mining and knowledge discovery in databases face such challenges that the discovered outputs are often not actionable. In the era of big data, how to effectively discover actionable insights from complex data and environment is critical. A significant paradigm shift is the evolution from data-driven pattern mining to domain-driven actionable knowledge discovery. Domain driven data mining is to enable the discovery and delivery of actionable knowledge and actionable insights. Domain driven data mining has attracted significant attention from both academic and industry. There was a workshop series on domain driven data mining during 2007-2014 with the IEEE International Conference on Data Mining and a special issue published by the IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering. There are also various new research problems and challenges in the last decade, where the incorporation of domain knowledge into data mining processes and models, such as deep neural networks, graph embedding, text mining, and reinforcement learning, is critically important.

explainer.lead: Domain driven data mining aims to turn findings from complex data into knowledge that people can actually act on. It brings domain knowledge into the mining process so that results are judged not just by whether they are interesting patterns, but by whether they support useful decisions.

tiers.eli5: Finding a pattern is a bit like noticing that students who forget their lunch often buy snacks. Domain driven data mining also asks what the school knows and what it can realistically do, such as adding lunch reminders, instead of stopping at an interesting observation. The goal is a discovery that leads to a helpful action.
tiers.practitioner: Apply it by incorporating domain knowledge into data preparation, models, and evaluation, including work with deep neural networks, graph embedding, text mining, and reinforcement learning. A key pitfall is treating a statistically strong pattern as useful without checking whether it fits the environment and supports a feasible action.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation, given complex data and behaviors D, domain knowledge K, and a complex environment E, domain driven data mining seeks knowledge p that is discovered from D, informed by K, and actionable within E. Its scope includes foundations, frameworks, algorithms, models, architectures, and evaluation systems for actionable knowledge discovery. A central limit of purely data-driven discovery is that its outputs may be valid patterns yet remain unusable in practice.

explainer.example: Suppose a retailer finds a pattern identifying customers likely to stop buying. Domain driven data mining would also consider which retention measures the retailer can realistically offer and evaluate the discovery by whether it supports such an action, rather than reporting the pattern alone.

usedIn.name: Text mining
usedIn.detail: Domain knowledge can be incorporated into text-mining processes and models to pursue actionable findings.

usedIn.name: Deep learning
usedIn.detail: Domain knowledge can guide deep neural networks rather than relying only on patterns learned from data.

usedIn.name: Graph embedding
usedIn.detail: Domain knowledge can inform graph-based representations and the assessment of discoveries.

usedIn.name: Reinforcement learning
usedIn.detail: Domain knowledge can be incorporated when learning from behavior in complex environments.

explainer.intuition: A pattern is not automatically useful merely because it appears in data. Domain driven data mining adds knowledge of the setting and its possible actions so discovery is directed toward insights that can be delivered and used.
howItWorks: Study complex data and behaviors together with knowledge of the domain.
Bring that domain knowledge into the mining process and models.
Discover candidate knowledge using suitable frameworks and algorithms.
Evaluate whether the findings are actionable, not merely statistically interesting.
Deliver actionable knowledge and insights for use in the environment.
explainer.whyItMatters: Data-driven pattern mining can produce outputs that are difficult or impossible to act on. With complex data and environments, combining discovery with domain knowledge helps close the gap between finding a pattern and delivering a useful insight.
misconceptions: It is not simply ordinary pattern mining with a larger dataset; the shift is toward domain-driven, actionable knowledge discovery.
A highly accurate or interesting pattern is not necessarily actionable.
Domain knowledge is not just added after mining to interpret results; it can be incorporated into the processes and models themselves.
